what_happened: The canonical spelling for 1a's promotion ('scope excursion', lowercase, single space) required no judgment call: it is already the literal --class string two independent, high-volume mechanical writers (git-commit-phase.sh:741 and git-commit-scoped.sh:866) emit today, and it accounts for 443 of the ~3800 total issues.jsonl lines scanned corpus-wide -- by far the single most common class value in the live corpus. Promotion is purely a documentation catch-up, not a new design decision.

The 17-class seed enum's 'kept in sync by hand' convention (noted only as a comment in issue-record.sh and orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh) has a wider blast radius than those two files: grep -rln '17-class|17 classes|seed enum' across agent-system/extensions/core/{scripts,context} surfaces 8 files carrying a numeral or list that goes stale on any seed-enum promotion (issue-log.md, issue-record.sh, orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh, conclusion-stage.md, phase-closure.md, orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh, error-recovery-strategies.md, orchestrate-batch-results-template.md). The plan for 1a should enumerate and update all 8, not just the 3 files that hold the actual class list.

Research report's 'promotion touches 8 files' figure re-validated against live state at plan time: grep -rn '17-class|17 classes' over agent-system/extensions/core/ returns 13 occurrences across 10 files, not 8. The two files the report omits are index-entries.json:3812 (the context-index summary string) and scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh:206 (an assertion message). Plan enumerates all 10.

Dispatch requirement 1d ('the three free-text examples must be caught by it') is not satisfiable by the research report's recommended post-fold token-count threshold of 6: research-confirmed-hypothesis folds to 3 tokens and reuse_of_existing_machinery to 4, so only reuse-not-reimplement confirmed by direct source read (8) exceeds it. Worked around in the plan by re-basing 1d's catch on issue-record.sh's existing outside-the-seed-enum stderr warning, which provably fires on all three, with the token-count check retained as an additional sharper signal.

common.sh's CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store environment override lets the real regression suite run against freshly-edited source-store scripts with no deploy in between (the suite copies the resolved script into a scratch .claude tree, so deploy-root-guard.sh still passes). Verified live at plan time: 15 passed, 0 failed at baseline. This turns what would have been three deploy-blocked phases into cheap local-tier phases.

Phase 1's verify-touched.sh narrowed-battery run (CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store) over this phase's 10 touched files selected test-common-lib.sh, which failed one case: 'mode=deploy-tree-first (both exist)' resolved the source-store fixture instead of the deployed one. Reproduced the failure in isolation with zero of this task's files involved -- running test-common-lib.sh alone with CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store exported fails the same case consistently (3/3), while running it with the env var unset passes consistently (3/3). The test's 'both exist' case does not guard against the ambient CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE override leaking into its own fixture call, which is designed to exercise plain deploy-tree-first behavior without the override. Pre-existing defect in lib/common.sh's test harness or test-common-lib.sh itself, outside this task's declared file_scope and unrelated to the seed-enum promotion this phase made.

While adding the usage-header documentation and SHARED FRAGILITY comment inside orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh's single-quoted jq script (--aggregate mode), an apostrophe in the phrase issue-record.sh's closed the enclosing bash single-quoted string early, producing a bash -n syntax error at the def fold_class line. Caught immediately by bash -n before any test run; fixed by rewording to avoid the apostrophe (issue_fold_class() helper inside issue-record.sh).

Phase 4's append-time warning design (fold-based seed membership + canonical-spelling warning + outside-enum warning extended to cite the new class-shape convention + token-count style warning) was verified directly against all three of the dispatch's named free-text examples plus the two canonical/non-canonical scope-excursion spellings in a single scratch pass before running the full suite, and every warning fired exactly as D2 predicted (token counts 3/4/8, with only the 8-token entry also triggering the style warning). The full test-issue-record.sh baseline (21 cases) stayed green with zero modification needed to the test file itself at this point -- the new warnings are purely additive to stderr and do not change any existing assertion's observable behavior.

Phase 5's new test-issue-record.sh case (s) initially grepped stderr for the literal substring 'class shape' (case-insensitive) to detect the new convention-citing warning, but the actual warning text reads 'Class Value Shape' convention (with 'Value' in between), so the substring never matched despite the warning firing correctly. Caught immediately on first test run (3 failures with clearly-matching warning text visible in the failure message); fixed by grepping for 'class value shape' instead.

For Phase 5's 10 new regression cases, rather than trusting the new assertions on faith, each one was independently proven non-vacuous: re-run against the pre-Phase-2/3/4 committed script versions (extracted via git show into a disposable scratch harness, never touching the live tree) confirmed 8 of the 10 genuinely fail on old behavior, and for the two directions no historical commit exhibits (the byte-identity hard constҕraint and the over-merge-rejection direction), a deliberately bug-injected scratch copy (a rewrite-on-read defect; a populated alias-table entry) confirmed those two would also catch a real regression. This is a cheap, repeatable technique (git show + scratch copy + direct re-run) worth reusing whenever a plan explicitly requires non-vacuous regression coverage.

Deploy-headless.sh's full verification pipeline (41 checks: contract compliance, state-writer boundary, orphan detection, shellcheck, and others) passed clean on the first attempt against all five phases' combined edits, including the auto-regenerated index-entries.json line_count correction. No deploy-stage rework was needed.

Phase 6's deploy-headless.sh regenerated index-entries.json's line_count field for every tracked context file, not just issue-log.md -- it also silently corrected git-staging-scope.md's line_count (1207 to 1211), a file squarely inside sibling task 567's declared file_scope, which had concurrently grown that file in an interleaved commit. Caught before committing by re-reading the full git diff rather than trusting the deploy output alone; split the single-file JSON diff by temporarily reverting the git-staging-scope.md hunk, committing only the issue-log.md correction under this task's own session, then restoring the git-staging-scope.md correction uncommitted in the working tree for task 567's own next commit to pick up. No foreign content was swept into this task's commit despite both corrections landing in the same physical file from one deploy run.

Task 477's postflight completion write was refused by the completion-deploy gate (exit 6): the deployed .claude/ tree was stale relative to the source store at completion time. Deferred to the next cycle's Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint to deploy and reconcile.
